title: A Nextcloud Flow webhook makes the sign-off survive the file being moved, renamed or deleted
content:
The integration uses Nextcloud Flow or a webhook, firing when a document reaches an approval state and dispatching a typed operation into Powerhouse. The claim being demonstrated is a survival property: the sign-off outlives the file being moved, renamed or deleted.

Those three verbs are chosen because they are ordinary file operations, not incidents. In a shared-file system documents get reorganised, renamed to match a convention and deleted when superseded, and none of that is misuse. If the approval lives only as a property of the file, ordinary housekeeping destroys the audit answer. Emitting the approval as its own record decouples the decision from the object's lifecycle.

Three leads carry this demo — one each in FR, DE and CH — all at "3 · later". The integration surface is a stock Nextcloud feature rather than custom code, so the build cost is low even though the cohort is cold.
